title: sharper deterministic prior (backoff char-LM + word-level) over the 43 prior-governed
hypothesis: a non-saturating backoff char-LM / word-level prior collapses the residual ambiguity of the 43 prior-governed free positions that the saturating hexagram left wide open (124)
insights: Sharper prior = stupid-backoff char-LM (maxn=7, non-saturating; the allowed char-LM class). Real-English 97-char windows score mean -0.54±0.10. Best joint-decode score -3.00 (-25.2σ vs English), word-coverage 72%. Over 60 restarts: 60 distinct decrypts (20 distinct among the top-20).

RESIDUAL AMBIGUITY head-to-head vs 124's saturating hexagram: per-position entropy of the PRIOR-GOVERNED 43 = 3.38 (all) / 2.84 (top-20) vs hexagram's 3.19; SELECTOR-LOCKED 30 = 1.15 / 0.97 vs hexagram's 1.08. The sharper prior does NOT collapse the 43: even a smooth non-saturating char-LM leaves the prior-governed positions highly ambiguous. The under-determination of the 43 is information-theoretic (the homophonic flattening destroyed the per-position signal), not a weakness of the hexagram floor.

WORD-LEVEL check: best decrypt segments 72% into dictionary words. Char-statistical fluency does not imply word-level English here; many distinct decrypts share similar char-LM scores -- the hallmark of genuine under-determination, not a scorer artifact.

VERDICT ON LEVER 1: a sharper deterministic prior does NOT break the 43; combined with 121-123 (selector mechanisms closed for the 30), NO admissible deterministic lever in hand resolves K4's free positions. The remaining levers are genuinely external (engraving layout / 5th positional crib, exp 126) -- not more priors or selector algebra.
next_steps: the 43 are information-theoretically under-determined by char-level priors too; Path A is effectively exhausted for unique recovery.
